mainTopic: Who bears the loss when sold wine sours or loses value: רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא's jug rule, רב חייא בר יוסף's view of מזל, and רבא's practical cases
overview: This amud opens with the end of the משנה, which explains what a seller owes when he promises 'spiced', 'old' or 'aged' wine. רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא says the משנה's rule (the seller is not responsible if wine sours) applies only when the wine was in the buyer's jugs. If the wine was still in the seller's jugs, the buyer can return it. The גמרא explains that this works when the buyer said he wanted the wine for cooking (מקפה). רבא shows that another line of the משנה forces this reading. רב חייא בר יוסף disagrees and holds that wine sours because of its owner's מזל. His פסוק about the haughty man leads to two lessons about arrogance. Next רבא gives practical rulings: a shopkeeper's barrel that sours partway through, with two limits, and wine sent to a port whose price drops on the way. The גמרא then asks what happens if that wine turns to vinegar, and gives two versions of the answer. Finally the גמרא quotes the משנה's line about 'old' wine to begin a new discussion.

steps.title: End of the משנה: promises about spiced, old and aged wine
steps.stepSummary: If the seller promised 'spiced' wine, it must last until עצרת (שבועות). 'Old' wine must be from last year, and 'aged' wine from three years back.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the seller said, 'I am selling you spiced wine,' he must make sure it lasts until עצרת. If he said 'old wine,' it must be from last year. If he said 'aged wine,' it must be from three years ago.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the end of the משנה. It lists special promises a seller can make about his wine, and what each promise obligates him to deliver.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally a seller is not responsible if wine turns sour after the sale. But when he uses words like 'spiced', 'old' or 'aged', he is promising a certain quality, and he must deliver what those words mean.

keyTerms.meaning: Spiced wine, made to keep well for a long time
To keep it standing, meaning to make sure the wine stays good
Another name for the festival of שבועות
Last year
Aged; here it means wine three years old

phrases.english: "…spiced [wine] I am selling to you"
he is obligated to keep it good for him until Atzeret.
phrases.notes: עצרת here means the festival of שבועות.

phrases.english: And [if he said] "old", it must be from last year's [wine],
and [if he said] "aged", it must be from three years [back].

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continuation of the משנה that began just before this section
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Promising spiced wine obligates the seller to make it last until עצרת. 'Old' means last year's wine, and 'aged' means wine from three years earlier.
steps.whatToRemember: Special descriptive words in a sale create real obligations for the seller.

steps.title: רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא limits the משנה to the buyer's jugs
steps.stepSummary: The rule that the seller is not responsible for souring applies only when the wine was in the buyer's jugs. If it was in the seller's jugs, the buyer can return it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא said: The משנה's rule (the seller isn't responsible if the wine turns sour) only applies when the wine was in the buyer's jugs. But if it was in the seller's jugs, the buyer can say, 'Here is your wine and here is your jug. Take them back.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins. רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא narrows the משנה's rule so that it covers only wine stored in the buyer's own containers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the wine soured in the buyer's jugs, the seller can blame the jugs. If it soured in the seller's own jugs, the problem seems to come from the wine itself, so the buyer can cancel the sale.

keyTerms.meaning: They only taught this in the case of… (a formula that limits a rule)
Jugs or jars used to store wine
The buyer
The seller
Your wine

phrases.english: GEMARA
Rabbi Yosei son of Rabbi Chanina said:
They only taught [this] about the buyer's jugs,
phrases.notes: 'This' is the משנה's rule that the seller isn't responsible when the wine turns sour.

phrases.english: but in the seller's jugs,

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לֵיהּ: הָא חַמְרָךְ וְהָא קַנְקַנָּךְ.
phrases.english: he can say to him: Here is your wine and here is your jug.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the משנה's earlier rule about wine that turns sour
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The seller is free of responsibility only when the wine soured in the buyer's jugs. In the seller's jugs, the buyer may return it.

steps.title: Challenge: why should the seller's jugs make a difference?
steps.stepSummary: Even in the seller's jugs, the seller could say: you shouldn't have left the wine there so long.
steps.simpleTranslation: But even if it was in the seller's jugs, so what? Let the seller tell him: 'You shouldn't have kept it so long!'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא's distinction between the buyer's jugs and the seller's jugs.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Wine doesn't last forever. If the buyer waited a long time before using it, the souring could be his own fault, whoever's jugs it sat in. So why should the seller have to take it back?

keyTerms.meaning: What of it? So what?
Let him say to him
To leave it waiting, to delay

phrases.english: And if it is in the seller's jugs, what of it?

phrases.aramaic: לֵימָא לֵיהּ: לָא אִיבְּעִי לָךְ לְשַׁהוֹיֵי!
phrases.english: Let him say to him: You should not have left it so long!

steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא's ruling that the buyer can return wine that soured in the seller's jugs
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The buyer's delay could be the cause of the souring, so the seller should not be responsible even in his own jugs.

steps.title: Answer: the buyer said he was buying it for cooking
steps.stepSummary: The ruling applies when the buyer told the seller he wanted the wine for a cooked dish, so it was clear he would keep it a long time.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, the ruling is needed for a case where the buyer told the seller he wanted the wine for cooking.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by placing רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא's ruling in a specific case: the buyer said the wine was for cooking.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A cooked dish uses only a little wine at a time, so the wine has to keep for a long while. Since the seller knew this, he cannot complain that the buyer waited too long.

keyTerms.meaning: It is only needed for… (introduces the exact case where a rule applies)
A thick cooked dish; wine for it is used a little at a time

phrases.english: No, it is needed
where he told him [it was] for a cooked dish.
phrases.notes: Wine for cooking is used slowly, so both sides understand it must last a long time.

steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought the seller could always blame the buyer for waiting too long.
steps.terutzMaskana: When the buyer said it was for cooking, long storage was expected, so wine that sours in the seller's jugs can be returned.
steps.confusionAlert: The cooking detail answers only the 'you waited too long' complaint. The jug detail still decides who gets the blame for the souring.

steps.title: Why not read the משנה in a simpler way?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא read the משנה as the buyer's jugs with a cooking request. He could have read it as the seller's jugs with no cooking request.
steps.simpleTranslation: What pushed רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא to explain the משנה as talking about the buyer's jugs, in a case where the buyer said it was for cooking? Let him explain it as the seller's jugs, where the buyer did not say it was for cooking!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions why רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא chose a more complicated reading of the משנה. This sets up an answer that will come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה's rule is that the seller is not responsible. That would make sense in the seller's jugs too, as long as the buyer never said 'for cooking', because then the seller can blame the delay. So why limit the משנה to the buyer's jugs?

keyTerms.meaning: What forced him? Why did he need to say this?
To set it up as, to explain it as talking about a certain case
Our משנה

phrases.aramaic: וּמַאי דּוּחְקֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי חֲנִינָא
phrases.english: And what forced Rabbi Yosei son of Rabbi Chanina
to explain our Mishnah as talking about the buyer's jugs
and where he told him [it was] for a cooked dish?
Let him explain it as the seller's jugs,
and where he did not tell him [it was] for a cooked dish!

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמַאי דּוּחְקֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי חֲנִינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the answer in step 4, the גמרא questions why רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא chose this reading at all
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא's choice to set the משנה in the buyer's jugs, even with a cooking request
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A simpler setting (seller's jugs, no cooking request) also explains why the seller is not responsible, so the narrower reading seems unnecessary.
steps.whyThisMatters: This question asks what forced a particular reading of the משנה. It sets up the next answer, which will explain what drove רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא.

steps.title: רבא shows the משנה itself forced the cooking reading
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers the question from Step 5. The later line of the משנה says that if the seller's wine is known to sour, the sale is a mistake. That only works if the buyer said he wanted the wine for a cooked dish.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: The משנה was hard for him, because it teaches: 'If it is known that his wine sours, it is a mistaken sale.' Why? The seller could say, 'You shouldn't have left it so long!' So we must learn from this that the buyer told him it was for a cooked dish. Yes, learn from it.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא explains why רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא had to add the detail that the buyer asked for cooking wine. A later line in the משנה makes no sense without it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says that if this seller's wine is known to go sour, the buyer can cancel the sale. But the seller could always say, 'You waited too long.' The only way the buyer wins is if he told the seller up front that he planned to keep the wine a long time, for a cooked dish. So the cooking detail comes from the משנה itself, not from guesswork.

keyTerms.meaning: A mistaken sale. The sale can be cancelled.
To leave something sitting for a long time
A thick cooked dish. Here it means wine bought to use in cooking over a long time.
Learn from it. Used both as a question and as a confirmation.

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the cooking condition is built into the משנה's own wording, so it is not an extra assumption.

phrases.english: Rava said: The Mishnah was difficult for him,
as it teaches: If it is known that his wine sours,
this is a mistaken sale.
Why? Let him say to him:
phrases.notes: The seller is speaking to the buyer.

phrases.english: You should not have left it so long!
Rather, isn't it so that we learn from this
that he told him it was for a cooked dish?
Yes, learn from it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 5's question about why רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא chose the cooking reading.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Textual necessity: a later line of the משנה requires the cooking condition.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We might have thought the משנה could be about the seller's jugs with no cooking request.
steps.terutzMaskana: The line 'if his wine is known to sour, it is a mistaken sale' only works if the buyer said it was for cooking. So the cooking condition is required.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The משנה is speaking about a buyer who told the seller he wanted the wine for a cooked dish.

steps.title: רב חייא בר יוסף says sour wine is the owner's bad luck
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא notes that רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא's view disagrees with רב חייא בר יוסף. He holds that wine sours because of its owner's מזל, so the seller cannot be blamed.
steps.simpleTranslation: This disagrees with רב חייא בר יוסף, who said: Wine sours because of its owner's fortune, as it says: 'And also, wine is treacherous, a haughty man...'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that another אמורא sees things differently. רב חייא בר יוסף says that if wine goes sour, it happens because of the owner's own bad מזל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא lets the buyer blame the seller when the wine sours. רב חייא בר יוסף holds that once the wine belongs to the buyer, its souring is the buyer's own fortune, so the seller is not at fault. He supports this with a פסוק that ties treacherous wine to a haughty owner.

keyTerms.meaning: And it disagrees. The גמרא is noting that two views clash.
The fortune (מזל) of its owner
Causes
Betrays, acts treacherously

phrases.english: And it disagrees with Rav Chiyya bar Yosef,
phrases.notes: 'It' is רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא's ruling that the buyer can blame the seller.

phrases.english: as Rav Chiyya bar Yosef said:
Wine: the fortune of its owner causes it to sour,
as it is said: "And also, wine is treacherous,
a haughty man, etc."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After confirming רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא's reading, the גמרא notes an opposing view.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Wine sours because of the owner's מזל, so the seller is not blamed once the wine belongs to the buyer.

steps.title: A haughty person is not accepted even at home
steps.stepSummary: רב מרי uses the same פסוק to teach that even the people in a haughty person's own house do not accept him.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב מרי said: A haughty person is not accepted even by the people of his own house, as it says: 'A haughty man will not abide.' What does 'will not abide' mean? Not even in his own home.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves from the legal discussion into a lesson drawn from the same פסוק. רב מרי teaches about the cost of arrogance.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word יִנְוֶה sounds like נָוֶה, which means a home or dwelling. So רב מרי reads the פסוק as saying the haughty man has no place even in his own home, because his family does not accept him.

keyTerms.meaning: Haughty, arrogant
The people of his household
Abide, dwell (from the פסוק)
Home, dwelling

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב מָרִי: הַאי מַאן דִּיהִיר –
phrases.english: Rav Mari said: Someone who is haughty
is not accepted even by the people of his own house,
as it is said: "A haughty man, and he will not abide"
What does "and he will not abide" mean?
Not even in his own home.
phrases.notes: He reads יִנְוֶה as coming from נָוֶה, a home.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב מָרִי: הַאי מַאן דִּיהִיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the פסוק quoted by רב חייא בר יוסף and explains it in a new way.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A haughty person is not accepted even by his own household.

steps.title: A pretend scholar is kept out of God's presence
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה in the name of רב teaches that someone who shows off by wearing the cloak of a תלמיד חכם, when he is not one, will not be brought into the presence of הקדוש ברוך הוא. He learns this by matching the word נוה in two פסוקים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of רב: Anyone who shows off in the cloak of a תלמיד חכם but is not a תלמיד חכם is not brought into the presence of הקדוש ברוך הוא. It is written here, 'and he will not abide (יִנְוֶה),' and it is written there, 'to Your holy dwelling (נְוֵה).'
steps.whatsHappening: A second lesson from the same פסוק. Pretending to be a Torah scholar is a kind of arrogance, and the pretender is kept out of God's holy place.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב connects יִנְוֶה in חבקוק with נְוֵה קׇדְשֶׁךָ, 'Your holy dwelling,' in שמות. So 'the haughty man will not abide' becomes 'he will not enter God's holy dwelling.' The haughty man here is someone who dresses like a תלמיד חכם without truly being one.

keyTerms.meaning: Shows off, takes pride
A cloak or garment
A Torah scholar
His area or presence (here, God's)
It is written here, and it is written there. A way of linking two פסוקים through a shared word.

steps.whatToRemember: The legal discussion ends with רבא proving the cooking reading from the משנה. רב חייא בר יוסף disagrees: souring is the owner's מזל. His פסוק about the haughty man leads to two lessons: a haughty person is rejected at home, and a pretend scholar is kept out of God's presence.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Rav said:

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל הַמִּתְגָּאֶה בְּטַלִּית שֶׁל תַּלְמִיד חָכָם,
phrases.english: Anyone who shows off in the cloak of a Torah scholar
but is not a Torah scholar
is not brought
into the presence of the Holy One, Blessed be He.
It is written here: "and he will not abide"
and it is written there: "to Your holy dwelling."

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב: כׇּל הַמִּתְגָּאֶה בְּטַלִּית שֶׁל תַּלְמִיד חָכָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives another reading of the same words, 'and he will not abide.'
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Someone who falsely presents himself as a תלמיד חכם is not brought into the presence of הקדוש ברוך הוא.

steps.title: Wine given to a shopkeeper that sours partway through goes back to the seller
steps.stepSummary: רבא rules that if a seller gave a shopkeeper a barrel of wine to sell by the cup, and it soured when half or a third was left, the seller must take the rest back.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Someone sold a barrel of wine to a shopkeeper so the shopkeeper could serve it out to customers. The wine soured when half or a third of it was still left. The law is that the seller must take the leftover wine back from the shopkeeper.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new practical ruling from רבא about wine that spoils while a shopkeeper is still selling it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The deal was that the shopkeeper would serve the wine out to customers. When it soured in the middle, the shopkeeper could not finish selling it. So רבא puts the loss of the leftover wine on the seller, not on the shopkeeper.

keyTerms.meaning: A barrel of wine
A shopkeeper
With the understanding that he would serve it out (sell it by the cup)
It turned sour
The law is that he must accept it back

phrases.english: Rava said:
This one who sells
a barrel of wine to a shopkeeper
with the understanding that he will serve it out,
phrases.notes: He means the shopkeeper will sell it to customers cup by cup.

phrases.english: and it soured at half or at a third,
the law is that he accepts it back from him.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: הַאי מַאן דְּזַבֵּין לֵיהּ חָבִיתָא דְחַמְרָא לְחַנְוָאָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns from the stories about haughty people (Steps 8-9) to the topic of wine that sours.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When wine given to a shopkeeper to serve out sours partway through, the seller must take the leftover wine back.

steps.title: Two limits on the shopkeeper ruling: the tap and market day
steps.stepSummary: רבא's ruling only applies if the shopkeeper did not change the barrel's tap and if market day had not yet arrived.
steps.simpleTranslation: We only said the seller takes the wine back when the shopkeeper did not change the tap. If he changed the tap, the seller does not take it back. And we only said it when market day had not come yet. If market day had come, the seller does not take it back.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא narrows רבא's ruling from Step 10 by adding two cases where the seller does not have to take the wine back.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule from Step 10 is not automatic. If the shopkeeper changed the tap, the seller does not take the wine back. If market day came while the wine was still good, the shopkeeper had his chance to sell it, so the loss stays with him.

keyTerms.meaning: We only said this when..., the formula that limits a ruling
He changed the tap of the barrel
Market day, when many customers come to buy

steps.confusionAlert: Both לָא lines mean the seller does NOT have to take the wine back. In those cases the shopkeeper keeps the loss.

phrases.english: And we only said this
where he did not change the tap,
but if he changed the tap – no.
And we only said this
where market day had not arrived,
but if market day arrived – no.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלָא אֲמַרַן אֶלָּא דְּלָא שַׁנִּי בְּבַרְזָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds two limits to the ruling in Step 10.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The seller takes the soured wine back only if the shopkeeper did not change the tap and market day had not yet arrived.
steps.whatToRemember: Seller takes back soured wine from the shopkeeper, but not if the tap was changed or market day already came.

steps.title: Wine sent to be sold at a port that drops in price before arriving
steps.stepSummary: רבא rules that if someone took wine to sell only at the port of ווֹל שָׁפָט, and the price dropped before he got there, the owner of the wine takes the loss.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא also said: Someone received wine on the understanding that he would bring it to the port of ווֹל שָׁפָט. By the time he got there, the price had dropped. The law is that the owner must accept the loss.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second ruling from רבא, this time about a middleman carrying wine to sell at a far-off port.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The deal set the place of sale: ווֹל שָׁפָט. The middleman did what was agreed, and the price simply dropped. So the drop in price is not his fault, and the owner of the wine takes the loss.

keyTerms.meaning: Who received wine (to sell for the owner)
A port
It became cheap; the price dropped

phrases.english: And Rava said:
This one who receives wine
with the understanding that he will bring it
to the port of Vol Shefat,
and by the time he arrived there, it became cheap;
the law is that he accepts it.
phrases.notes: The one who "accepts" here is the owner who gave the wine; he takes the loss.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רָבָא: הַאי מַאן דְּקַבֵּיל חַמְרָא אַדַּעְתָּא דְּמַמְטֵי לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second, separate ruling from רבא about wine that loses value.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If the price drops before the middleman reaches the agreed port, the owner of the wine takes the loss.

steps.title: What if the wine turned to vinegar on the way?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether, in רבא's port case, the owner also takes the loss if the wine turned to vinegar before it got there.
steps.simpleTranslation: They asked: If the wine turned into vinegar, what is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a question about the port case from Step 12. It is setting up the answers that come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A drop in price is clearly not the middleman's fault. Wine turning to vinegar is less clear, because Step 7 showed a disagreement over who is to blame when wine sours. So the גמרא asks if the owner takes this loss too.

keyTerms.meaning: They asked; a question raised in the study hall
Vinegar

phrases.english: It was asked of them:
If it became vinegar, what?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends the port case of Step 12 to wine that turns to vinegar.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does the owner of the wine also take the loss when the wine turns to vinegar before reaching the port?

steps.title: רב כהנא: the owner does not take the loss for vinegar
steps.stepSummary: רב הלל tells רב אשי that רב כהנא taught that the owner does not take the loss if the wine turned to vinegar, against the view of רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הלל said to רב אשי: When we were in רב כהנא's study hall, he told us: If it became vinegar, the owner does not take the loss. And this is not like רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a first answer to the question from Step 13, reported from רב כהנא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב כהנא splits the cases: a drop in price falls on the owner, but vinegar does not. He says openly that this goes against רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא, who let the buyer return wine that soured while still in the seller's jugs (Steps 2-6).

keyTerms.meaning: When we were in רב כהנא's study hall
And this is not like (a certain opinion)

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב הִלֵּל לְרַב אָשֵׁי:
phrases.english: Rav Hillel said to Rav Ashi:
When we were in Rav Kahana's study hall,
he said to us:
Vinegar – no,
phrases.notes: He means the owner does not have to take the loss when it turned to vinegar.

phrases.english: and this is not like Rabbi Yosei son of Rabbi Chanina.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב הִלֵּל לְרַב אָשֵׁי: כִּי הֲוַאן בֵּי רַב כָּהֲנָא
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The owner does not take the loss when the wine turns to vinegar; this goes against רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא.

steps.title: Another version: the owner takes the loss even for vinegar
steps.stepSummary: Others report that the owner takes the loss even if the wine turned to vinegar, following רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא.
steps.simpleTranslation: And some say: Even if it became vinegar, the owner also accepts the loss. Whose view is this? It follows רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second version of the answer to Step 13, which reaches the opposite result.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this version, vinegar is treated like a drop in price, and the owner takes the loss. The גמרא links this to רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא, who put the blame for souring on the seller's side. So the two versions in Steps 14 and 15 follow the two sides of the disagreement from Step 7.

keyTerms.meaning: Like whom? Whose opinion does this follow?

steps.whatToRemember: A price drop is on the owner of the wine. For vinegar there are two versions: רב כהנא says not on the owner (against רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא), and others say on the owner too (following רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא).

phrases.english: And there are those who say:
Even vinegar, he also accepts.
Like whom?
Like Rabbi Yosei son of Rabbi Chanina.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִיכָּא דְּאָמְרִי: אֲפִילּוּ חַלָּא נָמֵי מְקַבֵּל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different version of the answer in Step 14, with the opposite result.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The owner takes the loss even when the wine turns to vinegar, following רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא.

steps.title: Quoting the משנה about 'old' wine
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's rule that a seller who promises 'old' wine must give wine from the previous year, and abbreviates the rest of the line.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: If he sold 'old' wine, it must be from last year, and so on.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is quoting a new line from the משנה so it can start discussing it. This is a setup step that prepares the next move.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The topic shifts from רבא's cases about wine that went bad to the meaning of the word יָשָׁן in a sale. The משנה defines 'old' wine as last year's wine, so the seller must give at least that. The word כּוּ׳ tells us the quote continues past what is written here.

keyTerms.meaning: Old. Here it means wine from the year before.
Last year, the previous year.
Short for וְכוּלֵּי, 'and so on.' It tells you the quote continues.

phrases.english: 'Old' wine means wine from last year, etc.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves away from רבא's rulings on wine that lost value (steps 10-15) and begins a new discussion based on the next line of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A seller who promises 'old' wine must provide wine from the previous year.
